title: Routing error in dev mode: TypeError: Cannot read property 'includes' of undefined (take two)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```
  Operating System:
      Platform: linux
      Arch: x64
      Version: #1 SMP Fri Apr 2 22:23:49 UTC 2021
    Binaries:
      Node: 18.2.0
      npm: 8.9.0
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: 6.11.0
    Relevant packages:
      next: 12.1.7-canary.48
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
```

### What browser are you using? (if relevant)

Chrome, but n/a 

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

n/a

### Describe the Bug

#16874 is still impacting users. I have a repro! If the network request to `/_next/static/development/_devPagesManifest.json` fails for any reason, the Next.js dev application crashes with:

```plaintext
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')
    at resolveDynamicRoute (router.js?8684:1314:16)
    at _callee$ (router.js?8684:969:31)
    at tryCatch (runtime.js?ecd4:45:16)
    at Generator.invoke [as _invoke] (runtime.js?ecd4:274:1)
    at prototype.<computed> [as next] (runtime.js?ecd4:97:1)
    at asyncGeneratorStep (_async_to_generator.js?0e30:23:1)
    at _next (_async_to_generator.js?0e30:12:1)
```

### Expected Behavior

Next.js should be resilient to that manifest failing to load.

I took a dive into the source code and there are some _spicy_ TypeScript shenanigans happening 😄. And some TODOs about handling this correctly! #38046 is a draft PR showing what I'd suggest doing to resolve this issue.

1. The crash is coming from inside the framework, on [`if (pages.includes(fsPathname))`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/252d3b72f4f52b4308873ce7ad88be030d434df9/packages/next/shared/lib/router/utils/resolve-rewrites.ts#L89)
2. [`pages` is a parameter of `resolveRewrites`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/252d3b72f4f52b4308873ce7ad88be030d434df9/packages/next/shared/lib/router/utils/resolve-rewrites.ts#L12)
3. In calls to `resolveRewrites`, `pages` comes from [`this.pageLoader.getPageList()`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/8019cf002a32af9fad22375faeb90ddc16764b83/packages/next/shared/lib/router/router.ts#L1159)
4. [`getPageList`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/8019cf002a32af9fad22375faeb90ddc16764b83/packages/next/client/page-loader.ts#L56) doesn't properly handle the case of [`fetch(.../_next/static/development/_devPagesManifest.json)`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/8019cf002a32af9fad22375faeb90ddc16764b83/packages/next/client/page-loader.ts#L66) failing: [`return this.promisedDevPagesManifest!`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/8019cf002a32af9fad22375faeb90ddc16764b83/packages/next/client/page-loader.ts#L79) has a `// TODO Remove this assertion as this could be undefined` comment

### Link to reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vercel-next-js-flnphe?file=pages%2Findex.tsx

_(really, any Next.js app with a `Link` can demonstrate this issue)_

### To Reproduce

1. Start any Next.js app in development mode
2. Add a `<Link>` somewhere on the page
3. Visit localhost:3000 (or equivalent) in Chrome (or equivalent)
4. In the network tab, right click on the __devPagesManifest.json_ request and select _Block request url_
5. Refresh the page

Step 3 is the easiest way to simulate any of the reasons why that URL wouldn't be accessible that are mentioned in #16874. Apparently nginx configurations are more common culprits. Anecdotally I think I've seen this on CI runs that have flaky network layers (both GitHub Actions and CircleCI).
